beginner.headline: Anthropic Starts Selling Shares on the Stock Market
beginner.brief: People can now buy and sell shares in Anthropic on the stock market. Shares are small parts of a company. Anthropic makes Claude, a popular artificial intelligence (AI) tool that can talk with people. The company started just five years ago. Its share price was set at $83 before trading began. The price rose to $111.53, but it fell later that day. Each share cost $97.17 at the end of the day. Some investors, people who put money into companies, said the first day seemed to be a success. The price changes seemed to show that investors were still unsure about the future of AI.

intermediate.headline: Anthropic's Stock Market Debut Tests Confidence in AI
intermediate.brief: Anthropic became one of the world's most valuable public companies after its shares began trading on the stock market. It was the first company focused entirely on artificial intelligence (AI) to become publicly listed, allowing people to buy its shares. Its valuation, or total market value, reached roughly $1.76 trillion. Its debut, or first appearance, on the Nasdaq stock exchange was an important test for an industry receiving huge investment. The share price quickly reached $111.53 before dropping to $97.17 by the end of the day. Although Anthropic's shares gained roughly 17% during the day, the wider technology market did not perform as well. A few major technology companies spent more than $1 trillion on developing AI in the last year alone. The rapid growth in investment has raised concerns about a financial bubble, when prices rise beyond a reasonable value. Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot, expects significant price swings, or large movements up and down. Neil Wilson said there was no obvious similar company to compare Anthropic with. In the US, several politicians have said they want rules to make sure AI tools are safe. The company, which makes the AI chatbot Claude, will face close attention as people question whether AI is worth its cost.

advanced.headline: Anthropic's Market Surge Tests Confidence in AI
advanced.brief: Anthropic began trading on the Nasdaq stock exchange on Thursday against a backdrop of enormous spending on artificial intelligence (AI). The company reached a market value of roughly $1.76 trillion, placing it among the world's most valuable publicly traded businesses. As the first purely AI company to be publicly listed, Anthropic created a test for the wider industry. Its shares initially climbed to $111.53 before retreating to close at $97.17. The shares moved above their $83 allocation price, the price set for their initial distribution to investors, signalling considerable enthusiasm for AI. The broader Nasdaq Composite Index, however, closed nearly 2.3% lower. Nevertheless, Anthropic, the company behind Claude, faces intense scrutiny over whether AI will justify the resources devoted to it. A handful of major technology companies collectively spent more than $1 trillion on the AI buildout in the previous year alone. The pace of this spending has fuelled fears that prices may be inflated by excessive optimism. Economist Richard Whittle cautioned that bubbles burst when confidence in a positive future weakens, rather than necessarily on the day of a major deal. Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot, expects substantial fluctuations in Anthropic's share price. Barringer warned that the initial exuberance, or unusually strong enthusiasm, would wear off. Investor strategist Neil Wilson said that Anthropic lacks an obvious peer against which its worth can be assessed. New laws governing AI tools are also a possibility. Some US politicians have indicated that they want AI tools to be safe and subject to guardrails, meaning limits intended to prevent harmful use. Donald Trump reiterated his opposition to robust regulation of AI, indicating resistance to substantial rules governing the technology. A bipartisan group of US lawmakers nevertheless formed a caucus, a group organised around a shared policy interest, to address AI regulation and safety. Anthropic executives, including co-founder Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in expressing fears that future AI could outsmart humans and potentially threaten humanity's survival. Despite having described its rapidly developing technology as potentially dangerous, Anthropic has made an exceptionally swift transition from start-up to public listing.
